key_insight: Introduce a diffusion-based soft reparameterization that maps categorical one-hot variables into a continuous diffusion process and uses the learned denoiser to obtain low-variance, pathwise gradients—bridging unbiased score-function estimators and biased continuous relaxations.
problem_solved: Optimizing objectives with categorical/discrete variables suffers from either high-variance score-function estimators or biased continuous relaxations; this paper provides a new reparameterization that reduces variance while controlling bias.
method: Define a forward diffusion (noising) process that smoothly embeds categorical one-hot vectors into a continuous space (simplex or embedding space) via a noise schedule.
Train/derive a denoising (reverse) model / score estimator that enables sampling and computing pathwise gradients through the continuous diffusion trajectory back to categorical logits.

Construct gradient estimators that use the denoiser/score to produce lower-variance, tunable-bias gradients for learning tasks (e.g., variational inference), trading off noise schedule and estimator bias.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical alternative for training models with categorical latents or discrete choices: lower-variance gradients and a controllable bias/variance trade-off can improve stability and performance in variational inference, discrete optimization, and generative modeling.
visual_elements: Diagram: forward diffusion of a one-hot vector into a continuous manifold and the learned denoising reverse path back to discrete categories.
Comparison chart: variance vs. bias for score-function estimators, continuous relaxations (e.g., Gumbel-Softmax), and diffusion-based reparameterization.
Flowchart: sampling + gradient computation pipeline showing where the denoiser provides pathwise gradients during learning.
Empirical plot: training curve or ELBO / accuracy vs. noise-schedule steps showing improved stability or reduced gradient variance.
paper_title: Categorical Reparameterization with Denoising Diffusion models
paper_authors: Samson Gourevitch, Alain Durmus, Eric Moulines, Jimmy Olsson, Yazid Janati
